sections.heading: Second-floor laundry on a small lot is a long, bent vent
paragraphs: Many close-in houses put the dryer on the second floor and send lint on a crooked path to a rear wall. Elbows pack. The closet stays hot. Humidity from that vent sits in the same small envelope as the leaking older trunks.

sections.heading: This page is the independent city — not the sprawling Census label
paragraphs: The City of Falls Church is small: Broad Street, Washington Street, Tinner Hill, and tight blocks of 1920s–60s houses. That is a different place from the huge “Falls Church” name that sprawls through Fairfax County. Short yards put returns close to the film that coats porches along Route 7. I-66 and the Beltway add brake dust. Street trees add pollen. Returns pull all of it.
A house that gained central air later often has trunks snaked through tight joist bays. Dust collects at those kinks. You wipe a register. The next commute week puts the film back.
